name: neutral-site-indoor-unders
theory: Neutral-site games played indoors are showcase events: kickoff classics, conference championships, and neutral-site bowls. Public money piles onto these marquee matchups and books shade the total up to meet it, which can leave the under live even after the shade. Filtering to neutral site, indoors, and a dome venue together defines that exact spot; in this data indoor games are all played in domes, so the three filters land on the same 69-40 record backtesting a broader neutral-site-plus-indoors screen finds, going 63.30% to the under across 109 decided bets for +20.7% ROI (p is approximately 0.011 in this backtest, close to the 0.014 found in the original analysis). The result holds up across the calendar (week 1 63.3%, weeks 2 through 13 63.6%, week 14 and later 63.0%) and across eras (58.5% from 2013-2019 on 53 bets, 67.9% from 2020-2025 on 56 bets), which argues against this being a bowl-season fluke. Treat it as a lead, not an edge: 109 games is a small sample, and this finding was one of roughly 25 situational splits tested in the same analysis, so its p-value does not survive a Bonferroni correction across that full set (alpha near 0.002). It is also seasonally rare and clustered in a handful of weeks, so do not expect it to surface a match most weeks of the year.
